questions.prompt: In which order does light pass through the eye?
questions.explanation: Light enters through the cornea, passes the pupil, is focused by the lens, and lands on the retina.
questions.misconception: The order matters - light always enters at the front (cornea) and ends at the back (retina), not the reverse.

options: The size of the pupil, and how much light enters
The length of the optic nerve
questions.explanation: The colored iris is a muscle ring that opens and closes the pupil to control how much light enters.
questions.misconception: The iris is not about blood or nerve length - it is a light-regulating muscle around the pupil.

options: Light-sensing cells turn light into signals
questions.explanation: The retina is lined with light-sensing cells that convert light into nerve signals.
questions.misconception: The retina does not store light or 'see' by itself - it converts light into signals for the brain.

questions.prompt: Where does the image actually form?
options: In the brain, from the signals the eye sends
questions.explanation: The eye sends signals along the optic nerve, and the brain builds the picture you see - sight happens in the brain.
questions.misconception: You don't 'see' with the eyeball alone - the retina sends signals and the brain turns them into an image.

options: Makes the eye see color only
questions.explanation: The flexible lens bends the incoming light so it focuses sharply on the retina.
questions.misconception: The lens isn't a simple on/off gate - it focuses light precisely so the image is sharp.
